mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly FEDFUNDS rate above the prior 6 months' average predicts a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to tightened discounting of future cash flows.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative in at least 70% of FEDFUNDS-tightening events, or the 6-month moving average crossover is not cleanly detected.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 5% for two consecutive months, labor market slack increases, reducing equity risk premia and driving positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Over 60-day horizon, returns are negative in >50% of UNRATE-loosening events, or the 5% threshold is not met for two consecutive months in practice.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in HOUST (units of housing starts) accompanied by a decline in INDPRO (industrial production) signals demand-supply imbalance favoring demand, predicting positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative in >40% of such demand-supply cross events, or the cross is not statistically significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained quarterly decline in GDPC1 (real GDP) of at least 2% predicts negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns as investors anticipate contraction and lower earnings growth.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are non-negative in >50% of such GDP contractions, or the 2% threshold is not met in 3 consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 2% for three consecutive months, the low-rate environment supports equity valuation expansion, producing positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative in >60% of such low-rate episodes, or the 2% threshold is not maintained for three months in practice.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in PAYEMS (employment) by 2% in a month is followed by a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates labor market softening and reduced wage pressure.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are negative in >75% of such employment drops, or the threshold is not met in at least 5% of observations.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly CPIAUCSL inflation readings above 2.5% trigger a negative 20-day S&P 500 return as investors anticipate rate hikes and disinflation fears.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are non-negative in >50% of such inflation spikes, or the threshold is not met in 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A two-month decline in RSAFS (commercial loan growth) signals credit tightening, which predicts negative 60-day S&P 500 returns as credit availability shrinks.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are negative in less than 30% of such credit contraction episodes, or the 2-month decline is not observed in 5 consecutive months.
